---
title: "Lab 08 — Controlling for confounders"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("../R/lab_submission.R")
aid <- read_csv("data/aid_observational.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab08", title = "Controlling for confounders")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "In this teaching file, the naive aid coefficient is…",
  q2 = "After adding need, conflict, and institutions, the aid coefficient…",
  q3 = "A confounder is…",
  q4 = "Why is \"we controlled for everything\" not a causal proof?"
)
```

## What you will do

Compare a naive association with an adjusted one. Adjustment is not a design. Download the `.txt`.

```{r coefs, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=8}
m1 <- lm(economic_growth_pct ~ aid_per_capita, data = aid)
m2 <- lm(
  economic_growth_pct ~ aid_per_capita +
    baseline_need + conflict_intensity + institutional_quality,
  data = aid
)
c(naive = coef(m1)[["aid_per_capita"]], adjusted = coef(m2)[["aid_per_capita"]])
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("Negative (about -0.02).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Positive (about +0.04)."),
  answer("Exactly zero."),
  allow_retry = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Changes sign and becomes positive (about +0.04).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Stays negative and identical."),
  allow_retry = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("A common cause of treatment and outcome that can distort a raw comparison.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Any variable you can add to a regression."),
  answer("The residual."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(lab_prompts[["q4"]], open_answer(), trim = TRUE)
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}

  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),

    write_lab_submission(

      name = input$student_name,

      state = shiny::reactiveValuesToList(learnr::get_tutorial_state()),

```
